title: Maximal Orbital Entanglement from Non-Interacting Fermions
authors: Damiano Aliverti-Piuri, Julia Liebert, Christian Schilling
abstract: Orbital rotations are used in quantum many-body physics and chemistry to reduce the complexity of quantum states by compressing their correlation into a small set of relevant orbitals. In striking contrast, quantum information processing strives for the opposite: orbitals that maximize entanglement as a resource. Motivated by this, we prove that Slater determinants of $N$ fermions on a lattice of $d_A + d_B = d$ sites, although free of particle correlation, can carry up to $\min\{d_A, d_B, N, d-N\}$ ebits of orbital entanglement. Given enough particles and holes, this equals the maximum over all fermionic states. For arbitrary free states, we derive the maximal orbital total correlation in closed form for all bipartitions, the finest partition, and all partitions of up to five sites, using new majorization relations for Hermitian matrices. Taken together, these results turn mean-field states, the starting point of most many-body methods in physics and chemistry, into a viable resource for quantum information processing.
summary: This work determines the maximum amount of orbital entanglement extractable from non-interacting fermionic states using orbital rotations. By calculating this entanglement for various lattice partitions, the authors establish a quantitative link between mean-field quantum states and their potential utility as quantum information resources. This bridges a gap between condensed matter theory and quantum information science.
main_problem: The study aims to quantify the maximum orbital entanglement that non-interacting fermions, described by Slater determinants, can carry, contrasting this with the typical goal of minimizing correlation in many-body physics.
main_result: The maximal orbital entanglement for non-interacting fermions on a bipartite lattice is proven to be $\min\{\lambda_1, \lambda_2, N, d-N\}$ ebits, which equals the maximum over all fermionic states under certain conditions.
method: The analysis uses the 1-particle reduced density matrix formalism, deriving entanglement measures for various partitions and employing new majorization relations for Hermitian matrices.
model_or_system: The system consists of $N$ identical, spinless fermions on a bipartite lattice of $d$ sites, modeled by Slater determinants. The dynamics are governed by arbitrary one-particle (1P) unitary rotations.
key_observables: Orbital Entanglement Entropy ($E$), Orbital Total Correlation ($	ilde{C}_{\lambda}^{\max}$), and the 1-particle reduced density matrix (1RDM).
important_parameters: Number of fermions ($N$), total sites ($d$), and the partition sizes ($\lambda_1, \lambda_2$).
main_assumptions: The ability to apply arbitrary 1P unitary evolution ($u$) to the single-particle space is assumed for maximizing entanglement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the contrast between correlation minimization (QMB) and maximization (QI) via orbital rotations, and show the construction of optimal entangled states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by contrasting physical needs, derives the maximal entanglement for basic bipartite cases, and then generalizes the calculation to arbitrary partitions and correlation measures using advanced matrix theory.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, quantitative framework showing how mean-field states, typically viewed as approximations, can be engineered to serve as valuable, quantifiable resources for quantum information processing.

Figure 3. Representation of the orbitals involved in the con- struction of the optimal SD described in Result 1 for three fermions in a lattice of 6 + 4 sites.

Figure 4. Strategy for maximizing the orbital total correlation Cλ of a free state ρ over 1P unitaries U. (i) Restricting to free states allows us to map the problem from the 2d-dimensional Fock space to d × d 1RDMs γ whose eigenvalues equal the NONs n of ρ. (ii) Invariance under orbital rotations within each lattice region further reduces the problem to the 1RDMs’ block spectra b, which form a convex polytope Bλ n. (iii) The strictly Schur-concave objective function H is maximized by the majorization-least element of Bλ n. (iv) This element cor- responds to an optimal 1P unitary built with discrete Fourier transform-type unitaries.

Figure 5. A slice of the n-domain for d = 4 and λ = (2, 1, 1), for fixed n1 and n4. The blue, red, and green regions are slices of the first, second, and third regimes, respectively, as shown in Eq. (51). We emphasize the symmetry of the figure with respect to the line n2 + n3 = n1 + n4.
